<!-- BEGIN reference/guide.md -->
# Kinetic Construct (kinetic-serif v1.2.3) Authoring Guide

[Living design system](https://jeonkwan.github.io/kinetic-construct/) · [CSS](https://jeonkwan.github.io/kinetic-construct/css/kinetic-serif.css) · [Runtime](https://jeonkwan.github.io/kinetic-construct/js/kinetic-serif.js) · [JSON tokens](https://jeonkwan.github.io/kinetic-construct/reference/kinetic-serif.json)

## Philosophy & Communication Principles

1. **Information First**: Structure the explanation before selecting its visual presentation. Choose a diagram only when its relationships help answer the reader’s question. Name any trust perimeter or failure-mode claim explicitly.
2. **Strict Semantic 3-Role Accents (Botanical Field)**:
   - **Indigo (`#3730A3`)**: Blueprint, module source, definition, contract schema.
   - **Forest Moss (`#15803D`)**: Execution entry configuration, runtime boundary, active service, pipeline execution. Name the specific type: a root configuration is not itself a running service.
   - **Burnt Sienna (`#9A3412`)**: State storage, persistent ledger, database backend, immutable log.
   *Rule: Never use these three colors for arbitrary decoration.*
3. **Glare-Free Surfaces**:
   - Use `--bg-canvas: #F4F0E6` for viewport backdrops.
   - Use `--bg-surface: #FAF7F0` for elevated content cards.
   - Use `--bg-well: #EAE4D7` for recessed wells, code backgrounds, and callouts.
   - Use warm paper instead of pure white surfaces. Action foregrounds have their own contrast tokens.
4. **Locked Typography Contract**:
   - Display Headings: `Fraunces, Georgia, serif` (Weights 700-800, line-height 1.15-1.22).
   - Reading Prose: `Bitter, Georgia, serif` at `15px` (`0.9375rem`), line-height `1.55`, constrained to `max-width: 65ch`.
   - Technical & Code: `Fira Code, monospace` at `13px` (`0.8125rem`), line-height `1.55`.
   - Badges & Eyebrows: Strict floor of `13px` (`0.8125rem`). Never use sub-12px micro-text.
5. **Spatial Density & Layout**:
   - Navigation: Compact `220px` sticky left rail (`sidebar-rail`) that becomes a non-sticky, horizontally scrollable row at widths <= 960px; chapter labels do not wrap.
   - Flush Cards: Do not wrap sections in redundant outer container boxes with compound nested padding.
   - Side-Docked Workbench: On viewports > 960px, dock topology graphs side-by-side with code/contract inspectors (`1.25fr 1fr`).
   - Tactile Chrome: `2px solid #111111` borders with `2px 2px 0px #111111` shadows. Interactive elements translate `(2px, 2px)` on `:active`; their remaining shadow offset is `(1px, 1px)`. These are separate properties.


## Explanation and diagram authoring

Use the [representation selector and notation contract](diagram-guide.md) before drawing. Start with the reader's question, scope, evidence/assumptions, and one-sentence answer. The [complete topology specimen](../starter/diagram.html) demonstrates the accepted pattern: visible relationships before optional inspection, title/scope/caption/legend, a table equivalent, static HTML, and keyboard-operable detail. Its [Terraform/GCS assumptions](architecture-spec.md) are example-specific. Other diagram forms have selection advice only in this pilot.

Semantic accents apply to domain roles inside the figure. Editorial eyebrows and generic emphasis may remain neutral. Primary actions use `--action-bg` / `--action-ink` (light: `#15803D` / `#FAF7F0`; dark: `#34D399` / `#0E131B`); this action styling does not label a runtime node. Inspector selection uses a neutral outline plus check mark and `aria-pressed`; focus has a separate 3px outline with a 4px offset. The optional inspector uses buttons, not tab semantics. Its selected name is announced politely while focus stays on the initiating button.

CSS is the runtime token authority. JSON mirrors light tokens and includes dark overrides, action colors, diagram sizes, and interaction rules. Copy text is at least 13px; comment syntax colors are `#625D52` in light mode and `#8C9D97` in dark mode. Line numbers are decorative and must be `aria-hidden="true"` when used. No line-number dependency is used in the specimen.

Review comprehension separately from appearance: ask a reader to state the takeaway, explain all edges and boundaries, identify what is shared/separate/omitted, and name assumptions. Then check both themes, keyboard focus and state, no-JS meaning, print, and narrow/zoomed layouts. See the [pilot validation record](../docs/validation/2026-10-26-diagram-pilot.md) for what was actually tested.


## Agent use is opt-in

The companion skill applies only when explicitly selected/invoked or when the user clearly asks to use Kinetic Serif / Kinetic Construct. Generic explanation, documentation, or diagram requests do not activate it. Install `agents/openai.yaml` with `SKILL.md` to retain Codex's `allow_implicit_invocation: false` policy. Even after invocation, preserve the requested format and scope; a simple prose or Markdown answer does not become an HTML artifact unless the task asks for one.
<!-- END reference/guide.md -->

## Diagram selection and notation
Source: https://jeonkwan.github.io/kinetic-construct/reference/diagram-guide.md

<!-- BEGIN reference/diagram-guide.md -->
# Explaining relationships with Kinetic Serif

This is reusable authoring guidance. The [module/root/state specimen](../starter/diagram.html) demonstrates one topology. Its Terraform/GCS assumptions are recorded in [architecture-spec.md](architecture-spec.md); they are not universal design rules. Sequence, flowchart, and state diagrams below are selection advice, not implemented components in this pilot.

## Start with a brief

Write down the reader, the question they need answered, the scope, the evidence or assumptions, and a one-sentence takeaway. Reuse existing context instead of requiring a questionnaire. If the answer fits a sentence, start there. Add a visual when it makes a relationship easier to trace or compare.

## Choose a representation

| Reader needs to know | Start with | Check before drawing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What something means or why it matters | Prose and a concrete example | Would a graphic add anything? |
| How attributes or options compare | Table | Can readers compare the same attribute across rows? |
| What depends on or connects to what | Topology | Does every edge name its relationship and direction? |
| Who sends what, in what order | Sequence | Are actors, message order, and any waits explicit? |
| Which condition changes the path | Flowchart | Are branches labeled with conditions and outcomes? |
| Which states and transitions are possible | State diagram | Are nodes states, and transitions labeled with triggers or guards? |

Containment can show membership within a topology, but a folder, environment, administrative scope, and security boundary are different claims. Label the kind of boundary. A procedure is often clearer as numbered steps. Split a figure when the reader's question or abstraction changes, or the important path becomes hard to trace; no fixed node count is a cognitive law.

## The demonstrated figure contract

1. **Frame the answer.** A visible question, informative heading, scope line, and takeaway caption precede optional details. Name assumptions and omissions near the figure.
2. **Name each node.** Give it a type, readable name, stable identifier, and a concise responsibility in adjacent text. In the specimen, module means reusable source, root means an entry configuration used for execution, and state means persisted resource mapping. A root configuration is not a deployed service. Use a neutral treatment for actors or systems outside these roles. Classify by responsibility: an API schema is source/definition, a running API service is execution, a database is persisted state, and an external customer is neutral. A different subject may need a separately named role; do not assign a familiar color merely because a box needs emphasis.
3. **Name each edge.** Use subject → object, with a direct verb phrase. “Root → module: calls source” is a dependency; “root's Terraform run → state: reads/writes state” is an association aggregating access in both directions. The arrow identifies the subject and target; it is not packet direction, a complete data flow, or a timeline. Do not silently mix meanings.
4. **Name each boundary.** Dashed outlines in this specimen group environment configuration and its state association. They do not assert network or IAM enforcement, nor physical storage containment. Other boundary meanings require a new label and legend.
5. **Separate role from interaction.** Indigo/source, moss/root, and sienna/state retain their domain meanings. A check mark, neutral outline, and `aria-pressed` communicate inspector selection. A separate focus outline identifies keyboard focus. Generic primary actions use action tokens; green on a button does not label a root node. Warnings need explicit text, not a reused role color.
6. **Keep geometry readable.** Route orthogonal connectors with rounded elbows, attach them perpendicularly to nodes, separate routes, and place labels off their strokes with opaque masks. Use a stable reading order. Passive nodes have role borders; tactile shadows belong to controls and established card chrome.
7. **Provide an equivalent route.** Keep a visible relationship table or readable explanation with every essential edge, node type, scope, and caveat. Give the SVG a unique title and description. Do not rely on hover or the SVG description alone.

## Copy the pattern

Copy the marked `BEGIN module-state specimen` section from [starter/diagram.html](../starter/diagram.html), with the shared CSS and JS. The standalone page is the canonical specimen source. Its mirrored chapter in `index.html` is generated by `python3 sync_reference.py`.

The static figure uses `.diagram-figure`, `.diagram-scroll`, and `.relationship-diagram`. The 880 × 480 viewBox renders at a minimum width of 880 CSS pixels: prose labels are 15px, technical identifiers/type labels 13px, and Fraunces node names 20px. The SVG can grow on wider layouts. On narrow layouts it scrolls inside a keyboard-focusable labeled region; surrounding prose and the table reflow. Do not shrink all text to fit a phone. When duplicating a figure, change all SVG title/description/marker IDs, HTML detail IDs, and corresponding ARIA references to remain unique.

The optional native `<details>` inspector contains normal buttons grouped with `role="group"`. Each button's `data-node` matches one article's `data-detail`; `aria-controls` references its article ID. Runtime enhancement exposes the controls, selects the first node, sets exactly one `aria-pressed="true"`, hides other articles, and announces the selected name via a polite status. Tab reaches each button, Enter or Space selects, and focus stays on the button; Tab continues into visible code/copy controls. These are buttons, not tabs: arrow-key navigation is not promised. The check mark and `.selected` outline are independent of role colors.

Without JavaScript, selection controls stay hidden and all five code excerpts remain available inside native details. The overview, table, assumptions, and caption remain visible. Print keeps that same core lesson and omits the optional inspector. No animation is needed.

## Review meaning separately from appearance

First give only the page or its readable text to a fresh reader. Ask: What is shared? What stays separate? Explain every arrow. What does each dashed box claim? Which objects are actually deployed, and what was omitted? What conditions could invalidate the example? Then give an author only the distributed guide and specimen and ask them to reproduce the pattern. Record ambiguity and revise it before visual polish.

Separately inspect the rendered page: both themes, keyboard controls and focus/selection, normal text at least 4.5:1 and meaningful graphics at least 3:1 against adjacent colors, narrow widths/zoom, no JavaScript, and print. Test loaded fonts as well as fallbacks when available. Automated checks and an AI reader diagnostic do not replace a human usability or screen-reader study.

The local [research report](../docs/research/2026-10-26-information-design-review.md) records the source register and limitations behind these choices. These conventions adapt C4 notation and information-design heuristics; they do not adopt a complete C4 model or claim one visual form always outperforms a table.
<!-- END reference/diagram-guide.md -->

# Kinetic Serif diagram style profile

Project-local adaptation for the installed Diagram Design skill. This file is authoritative for this pilot's skin; it does not modify shared skill defaults. Use alongside [guide.md](guide.md) and [diagram-guide.md](diagram-guide.md).

- Paper roles: `--bg-canvas`, `--bg-surface`, `--bg-well`; ink: `--ink-primary`, `--ink-prose`, `--ink-muted` from the shared CSS, in both themes.
- Fraunces for display and node names; Bitter for readable labels/prose; Fira Code for technical identifiers and type labels. Rendered floors are 15px prose and 13px technical text at the diagram's minimum width.
- Source/module: `--accent-module` and its background; execution/root configuration: `--accent-root`; persisted state: `--accent-state`. Type labels preserve meaning without color. Neutral ink for edges and selection.
- Passive nodes: 2px role border, 6px radius, no button shadow. Existing tactile cards and controls retain Kinetic Serif shadows and 2px active translation.
- The pilot is an 880 × 480 configuration topology with five nodes and four edges, locally scrollable below 880px. This is a content/layout choice, not a universal complexity budget.
- Direct edge labels, rounded orthogonal routing, named dashed environment scopes, caption, legend, equivalent relationship table, and static HTML all precede optional inspection.
- No motion, added palette, default skill fonts, or new visual family is needed.
<!-- END reference/diagram-style.md -->

name: kinetic-serif
description: Apply the Kinetic Construct / Kinetic Serif design system only when the user explicitly invokes $kinetic-serif or asks to use this named design system. Preserve the requested output format and scope; generic documentation, diagram, typography, or explanation requests do not activate this skill.

# Kinetic Construct (kinetic-serif v1.2.3)

Create high-density, legible technical explainers and living architecture documentation using the calibrated Kinetic Construct design language.

## Invocation and output scope

This skill is opt-in. Activate it only when the user explicitly invokes `$kinetic-serif`, selects this skill, or clearly asks to apply **Kinetic Serif / Kinetic Construct**. An incidental mention, a request to inspect this skill, or a generic request for documentation, a diagram, typography, or a short explanation is not an instruction to apply it.

The companion `agents/openai.yaml` sets `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false` for Codex. Install the whole `reference/` directory as the skill folder so this policy accompanies `SKILL.md`. Hosts that do not support this policy must still follow the explicit-invocation boundary in these instructions.

Invocation selects the design language, not the deliverable format. Preserve the user's requested medium, complexity, and scope. A short prose answer stays short prose; a Markdown table stays Markdown. Create or modify HTML/CSS/JavaScript only when the user requests a web deliverable or the established task already requires one. Discussing a diagram does not automatically request a standalone interactive page.

Examples:
- “Use `$kinetic-serif` to build an HTML explainer” → apply the design system to the requested HTML.
- “Use Kinetic Serif to make a brief Markdown comparison” → give a brief Markdown comparison; create no webpage.
- “Explain modules versus state in two sentences” → ordinary prose; do not activate this skill.
- “What does the Kinetic Serif skill do?” → explain its behavior; do not start designing an artifact.

## Hosted References & Integration

Canonical site: [Kinetic Construct](https://jeonkwan.github.io/kinetic-construct/).

When authoring a guide in another project, use the published assets:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://jeonkwan.github.io/kinetic-construct/css/kinetic-serif.css" />
<script src="https://jeonkwan.github.io/kinetic-construct/js/kinetic-serif.js" defer></script>
```

The stylesheet imports Fraunces, Bitter, and Fira Code and defines the complete light/dark token contract. Read the [authoring guide](https://jeonkwan.github.io/kinetic-construct/reference/guide.md) for layout and semantic color rules and the [JSON tokens](https://jeonkwan.github.io/kinetic-construct/reference/kinetic-serif.json) for machine-readable values. Use the [starter HTML](https://jeonkwan.github.io/kinetic-construct/starter/index.html) as a structural example; when copying it to another project, replace its `../css/` and `../js/` references with the hosted URLs above, or copy those asset directories and adjust the paths to their local location.

- [Discovery manifest](https://jeonkwan.github.io/kinetic-construct/llms.txt): discover the published resources.
- [Complete prompt context](https://jeonkwan.github.io/kinetic-construct/llms-full.txt): ingest the consolidated guide, tokens, assets, starter, and specimen.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/Jeonkwan/kinetic-construct): inspect or download the maintained sources.

For offline use, bundle the CSS and JavaScript with the guide and provide the fonts locally if they are needed without internet access. The Pages URLs track the repository's latest deployed `main`; vendor assets from a chosen Git commit when a project needs a fixed revision.

## Core Design Contract & CSS Tokens

The hosted stylesheet includes the complete token set. The excerpt below records the core design values for reference and inline implementations:

```css
:root {
  --bg-canvas: #F4F0E6;       /* Warm Alabaster canvas */
  --bg-surface: #FAF7F0;      /* Elevated card surface */
  --bg-well: #EAE4D7;         /* Recessed code well */
  --ink-primary: #111111;     /* Primary chrome & heading ink */
  --ink-prose: #222222;       /* Body prose ink */
  --ink-muted: #4A4740;       /* Secondary captions */

  --accent-module: #3730A3;   /* Indigo: Blueprint / Module */
  --accent-module-bg: #E0E7FF;
  --accent-root: #15803D;     /* Forest Moss: Execution / Root Configuration */
  --accent-root-bg: #DCFCE7;
  --accent-state: #9A3412;    /* Burnt Sienna: State Ledger */
  --accent-state-bg: #FFEDD5;

  --border-thick: 2px solid var(--ink-primary);
  --shadow-tactile: 2px 2px 0px var(--ink-primary);
  --radius-subtle: 6px;

  --font-display: 'Fraunces', Georgia, serif;
  --font-prose: 'Bitter', Georgia, serif;       /* 15px / 0.9375rem */
  --font-mono: 'Fira Code', monospace;         /* 13px / 0.8125rem */

  --container-max: 1520px;
  --rail-width: 220px;
  --outer-gutter: clamp(12px, 1.8vw, 24px);
  --section-gap: 22px;
}
```


## Authoring workflow and accepted relationship pattern

1. Establish the reader, question, scope, evidence or assumptions, and one-sentence takeaway from supplied context. Choose prose for explanation, a table for comparison, topology for dependencies, sequence for ordered messages, flowchart for decisions, or state diagram for states/transitions. Only the topology is implemented in this pilot; do not invent a gallery or require Terraform chapters.
2. Read [diagram-guide.md](https://jeonkwan.github.io/kinetic-construct/reference/diagram-guide.md) for notation and the [project-local diagram style](https://jeonkwan.github.io/kinetic-construct/reference/diagram-style.md). Copy the marked section from [starter/diagram.html](https://jeonkwan.github.io/kinetic-construct/starter/diagram.html), the canonical accepted specimen source. Preserve its visible overview, scope, legend, takeaway, relationship table, assumptions, and no-JS path. Rename all IDs and ARIA references if adding another figure.
3. Use subject → object arrows with specific verb labels. Name node types and boundary kinds. Source/root/state colors are domain roles, not selection or status. Roots in the example are configurations used for execution, not running database instances. Use neutral styling for unrelated actors. Keep readable technical labels at least 13px and prose labels at least 15px at the minimum rendered SVG width; scroll the figure locally instead of shrinking it on mobile.
4. Treat [architecture-spec.md](https://jeonkwan.github.io/kinetic-construct/reference/architecture-spec.md) as an illustrative Terraform/GCS model with checked concepts and explicit assumptions. Do not claim distinct state implies IAM isolation, complete blast-radius protection, or a deployed system. The missing historical three-plane enumeration is unknown and must not be invented.
5. Preserve progressive enhancement: native details contains all code without JS. JS exposes grouped inspector buttons, shows one detail article, sets `aria-pressed`, adds a neutral selection outline/check, and announces the selected name. Tab/Enter/Space operate the controls; no arrow-key tablist behavior is promised. Core meaning remains outside interaction.
6. Test comprehension with a fresh reader independently of visual/functional checks. Ask for the conclusion, every edge's direction/meaning, boundary claims, omissions, and conditions. Inspect both themes, focus/selection, contrast, reflow/zoom, no JS, and print. State limits of automated or AI-reader checks.

## Contract details and distribution

- Mobile rail: non-sticky horizontal scrolling row at <= 960px; docked workbench above 960px.
- Tactile active translation: 2px on both axes; remaining active shadow: 1px on both axes.
- Generic primary buttons use separate action tokens: light background/ink `#15803D`/`#FAF7F0`, dark `#34D399`/`#0E131B`. Domain role colors do not indicate inspector selection.
- CSS is the runtime authority; JSON mirrors light values and dark overrides. The warm-surface preference does not forbid a separately tested action foreground.
- After changing the canonical specimen or bundled references, run `python3 sync_reference.py`, then `python3 sync_reference.py --check`. This mirrors the specimen into the showcase and regenerates `llms-full.txt`. Account for new distributable files in both `make_repo.py` and the browser runtime's file list; regenerate the ZIP for a current local download.

## Stylesheet
Source: https://jeonkwan.github.io/kinetic-construct/css/kinetic-serif.css

<!-- BEGIN css/kinetic-serif.css -->
/* ==========================================================================
   KINETIC CONSTRUCT (kinetic-serif v1.2.3)
   Core Design System Tokens, Typography Floors & Component Primitives
   ========================================================================== */

@import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Bitter:ital,wght@0,400;0,500;0,600;1,400&family=Fira+Code:wght@400;500;600&family=Fraunces:ital,opsz,wght@0,9..144,700..800;1,9..144,700&display=swap');

:root {
  /* Glare-Free Paper Surfaces & Ink (Warm Alabaster Default) */
  --bg-canvas: #F4F0E6;
  --bg-surface: #FAF7F0;
  --bg-well: #EAE4D7;
  --ink-primary: #111111;
  --ink-prose: #222222;
  --ink-muted: #4A4740;

  /* Botanical Field 3-Role Architecture Accents */
  --accent-module: #3730A3;
  --accent-module-bg: #E0E7FF;
  --accent-root: #15803D;

## Runtime
Source: https://jeonkwan.github.io/kinetic-construct/js/kinetic-serif.js

<!-- BEGIN js/kinetic-serif.js -->
/**
 * Kinetic Construct (kinetic-serif v1.2.3) Runtime
 * Manages theme toggling, node graph inspection, copy helpers,
 * and client-side zero-dependency ZIP archive creation.
 */

(function () {
  'use strict';

  const assetBase = new URL('../', document.currentScript.src);

  // 1. Theme Toggle
  window.toggleTheme = function () {
    const html = document.documentElement;
    const next = html.getAttribute('data-theme') === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark';
    html.setAttribute('data-theme', next);
    try { localStorage.setItem('kinetic-theme', next); } catch (_) { /* Storage may be disabled. */ }
    const btn = document.getElementById('themeToggleBtn');
    if (btn) btn.textContent = next === 'dark' ? '☀️ Daylight' : '🌙 Nocturnal';
  };

  let saved;
  try { saved = localStorage.getItem('kinetic-theme'); } catch (_) { /* Use the system preference. */ }
  if (saved) {
    document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme', saved);
  } else if (window.matchMedia && window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches) {
    document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme', 'dark');
  }

  const themeButton = document.getElementById('themeToggleBtn');
  if (themeButton) {
    themeButton.hidden = false;
    themeButton.textContent = document.documentElement.getAttribute('data-theme') === 'dark'
      ? '☀️ Daylight' : '🌙 Nocturnal';
  }

  // 2. Clipboard Copy Helper
  window.copySnippet = async function (btn, textToCopy) {
    const text = textToCopy || btn.closest('.code-wrapper').querySelector('.code-lines-col').innerText;
    const orig = btn.innerText;
    try {
      await navigator.clipboard.writeText(text);
      btn.innerText = 'Copied! ✓';
    } catch (_) {
      btn.innerText = 'Select code to copy';
    }
    setTimeout(() => { btn.innerText = orig; }, 1800);
  };

  // Progressive enhancement: the SVG, table, assumptions, and all code are HTML.
  // Buttons select optional detail; they do not carry the lesson's core meaning.
  document.querySelectorAll('[data-topology]').forEach(figure => {
    const controls = figure.querySelector('.inspector-controls');
    const status = figure.querySelector('.inspector-status');
    const buttons = [...figure.querySelectorAll('[data-node]')];
    const panels = [...figure.querySelectorAll('[data-detail]')];
    function inspect(button) {
      buttons.forEach(item => {
        const selected = item === button;
        item.classList.toggle('selected', selected);
        item.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(selected));
      });
      panels.forEach(panel => { panel.hidden = panel.dataset.detail !== button.dataset.node; });
      status.textContent = `Inspecting ${button.textContent}`;
    }
    buttons.forEach(button => button.addEventListener('click', () => inspect(button)));
    if (buttons.length) {
      inspect(buttons[0]);
      controls.hidden = false;
      status.hidden = false;
      figure.querySelectorAll('.copy-button').forEach(button => { button.hidden = false; });
    }
  });

  // 3. Topology Inspector Handler
  window.selectTopologyNode = function (btn, role, title, file, code, blastDesc) {
    const scope = btn.closest('[data-topology]') || document;
    scope.querySelectorAll('.node-btn').forEach(b => {
      b.classList.remove('selected');
      b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', 'false');
    });
    btn.setAttribute('aria-pressed', 'true');
    btn.classList.add('selected');

    const badge = document.getElementById('topologyInspBadge');
    if (badge) {
      badge.className = `role-badge ${role}`;
      badge.textContent = role === 'module' ? 'MODULE BLUEPRINT' : role === 'root' ? 'EXECUTION ROOT' : 'REMOTE STATE LEDGER';
    }

    const titleEl = document.getElementById('topologyInspTitle');
    if (titleEl) titleEl.textContent = title;

    const fileEl = document.getElementById('topologyInspFile');
    if (fileEl) fileEl.textContent = file;

    const codeEl = document.getElementById('topologyInspCode');
    if (codeEl) codeEl.textContent = code;

    const blastEl = document.getElementById('topologyInspBlast');
    if (blastEl) blastEl.textContent = blastDesc;
  };

  // 4. Decision Lab Engine
  window.calculateTopologyRecommendation = function () {
    const teamSize = document.getElementById('labTeamSize')?.value || 'small';
    const blastRisk = document.getElementById('labBlastRisk')?.value || 'standard';
    const resultCard = document.getElementById('labResultCard');
    if (!resultCard) return;

    if (teamSize === 'large' || blastRisk === 'strict') {
      resultCard.innerHTML = `
        <div class="role-badge state" style="margin-bottom: 8px;">ILLUSTRATIVE OPTION</div>
        <h3>Isolated Roots with Granular GCS State Boundaries</h3>
        <p>Deploy independent root configurations per service and environment with dedicated service accounts and separate state buckets to minimize blast radius.</p>
      `;
    } else {
      resultCard.innerHTML = `
        <div class="role-badge root" style="margin-bottom: 8px;">ILLUSTRATIVE OPTION</div>
        <h3>Lightweight Monorepo with Shared Modules</h3>
        <p>Maintain root configurations in a monorepo versioned by Git commit SHAs, referencing internal modules directly with change detection.</p>
      `;
    }
  };

  // 5. Zero-Dependency In-Browser ZIP Builder
  // Implements standard PKZip format using pure typed arrays
  function crc32(bytes) {
    let crc = 0xFFFFFFFF;
    for (const byte of bytes) {
      crc ^= byte;
      for (let bit = 0; bit < 8; bit++) {
        crc = (crc >>> 1) ^ ((crc & 1) ? 0xEDB88320 : 0);
      }
    }
    return (crc ^ 0xFFFFFFFF) >>> 0;
  }

  function createZip(files) {
    const fileEntries = [];
    let offset = 0;

    const encoder = new TextEncoder();

    files.forEach(file => {
      const nameBytes = encoder.encode(file.name);
      const dataBytes = typeof file.content === 'string' ? encoder.encode(file.content) : file.content;
      const size = dataBytes.length;
      const checksum = crc32(dataBytes);

      // Local File Header (30 bytes) + Name + Data
      const header = new Uint8Array(30 + nameBytes.length);
      const view = new DataView(header.buffer);
      view.setUint32(0, 0x04034b50, true);  // Local file header signature
      view.setUint16(4, 20, true);          // Version needed
      view.setUint16(6, 0x0800, true);      // UTF-8 filenames
      view.setUint16(8, 0, true);           // Compression: 0 (Store)
      view.setUint16(10, 0, true);          // Time
      view.setUint16(12, 33, true);         // Date: 1980-01-01
      view.setUint32(14, checksum, true);   // CRC32
      view.setUint32(18, size, true);       // Compressed size
      view.setUint32(22, size, true);       // Uncompressed size
      view.setUint16(26, nameBytes.length, true); // Name length
      view.setUint16(28, 0, true);          // Extra field length
      header.set(nameBytes, 30);

      fileEntries.push({
        nameBytes,
        header,
        dataBytes,
        offset,
        size,
        checksum
      });

      offset += header.length + dataBytes.length;
    });

    // Central Directory
    let centralDirSize = 0;
    const centralEntries = fileEntries.map(entry => {
      const cd = new Uint8Array(46 + entry.nameBytes.length);
      const view = new DataView(cd.buffer);
      view.setUint32(0, 0x02014b50, true);  // Central dir signature
      view.setUint16(4, 20, true);          // Made by
      view.setUint16(6, 20, true);          // Version needed
      view.setUint16(8, 0x0800, true);      // UTF-8 filenames
      view.setUint16(10, 0, true);          // Compression (Store)
      view.setUint16(12, 0, true);          // Time
      view.setUint16(14, 33, true);         // Date: 1980-01-01
      view.setUint32(16, entry.checksum, true); // CRC32
      view.setUint32(20, entry.size, true); // Compressed size
      view.setUint32(24, entry.size, true); // Uncompressed size
      view.setUint16(28, entry.nameBytes.length, true);
      view.setUint16(30, 0, true);          // Extra length
      view.setUint16(32, 0, true);          // Comment length
      view.setUint16(34, 0, true);          // Disk start
      view.setUint16(36, 0, true);          // Internal attrs
      view.setUint32(38, 0, true);          // External attrs
      view.setUint32(42, entry.offset, true);// Local header offset
      cd.set(entry.nameBytes, 46);
      centralDirSize += cd.length;
      return cd;
    });

    // End of Central Directory Record (22 bytes)
    const eocd = new Uint8Array(22);
    const eocdView = new DataView(eocd.buffer);
    eocdView.setUint32(0, 0x06054b50, true);  // EOCD signature
    eocdView.setUint16(4, 0, true);           // Disk number
    eocdView.setUint16(6, 0, true);           // Central dir disk
    eocdView.setUint16(8, fileEntries.length, true);  // Disk entries
    eocdView.setUint16(10, fileEntries.length, true); // Total entries
    eocdView.setUint32(12, centralDirSize, true);     // Central dir size
    eocdView.setUint32(16, offset, true);             // Central dir offset
    eocdView.setUint16(20, 0, true);                  // Comment length

    // Assemble parts into single Blob
    const parts = [];
    fileEntries.forEach(e => {
      parts.push(e.header);
      parts.push(e.dataBytes);
    });
    centralEntries.forEach(cd => parts.push(cd));
    parts.push(eocd);

    return new Blob(parts, { type: 'application/zip' });
  }

  // 6. Download Hub Trigger
  // Pages builds a complete archive because its artifact excludes hidden files.
  // On a local HTTP server, fall back to assembling all source files in-browser.
  const repositoryFiles = [
    '.github/workflows/pages.yml', '.gitignore',
    'css/kinetic-serif.css', 'js/kinetic-serif.js',
    'reference/kinetic-serif.json', 'reference/SKILL.md', 'reference/agents/openai.yaml',
    'reference/guide.md', 'reference/diagram-guide.md', 'reference/diagram-style.md',
    'reference/architecture-spec.md', 'starter/diagram.html', 'sync_reference.py',
    'docs/research/2026-10-26-information-design-review.md',
    'docs/validation/2026-10-26-diagram-pilot.md',
    'starter/index.html', 'index.html', 'llms.txt', 'llms-full.txt',
    'README.md', 'LICENSE', 'make_repo.py'
  ];

  window.downloadRepoZip = async function (btn) {
    const origText = btn.innerHTML;
    btn.disabled = true;
    btn.innerHTML = 'Compiling ZIP... ⏳';

    try {
      const archiveName = 'kinetic-construct-v1.2.3.zip';
      const response = await fetch(new URL(archiveName, assetBase));
      let blob;
      if (response.ok) {
        blob = await response.blob();
      } else {
        const files = await Promise.all(repositoryFiles.map(async path => {
          const result = await fetch(new URL(path, assetBase));
          if (!result.ok) throw new Error(`Could not fetch ${path}: HTTP ${result.status}`);
          return { name: `kinetic-construct/${path}`, content: await result.text() };
        }));
        blob = createZip(files);
      }

      const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
      const a = document.createElement('a');
      a.href = url;
      a.download = archiveName;
      document.body.appendChild(a);
      a.click();
      a.remove();
      setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 1000);

      btn.innerHTML = 'Downloaded! ✓';
      setTimeout(() => { btn.innerHTML = origText; }, 2200);
    } catch (err) {
      console.error(err);
      alert('Unable to download the complete repository. Serve this folder over HTTP, or run python3 make_repo.py to create the ZIP locally.');
      btn.innerHTML = origText;
    } finally {
      btn.disabled = false;
    }
  };

  // 7. Rail Scroll Sync
  window.addEventListener('scroll', () => {
    const sections = document.querySelectorAll('section[id]');
    const scrollPos = window.scrollY + 120;
    sections.forEach(sec => {
      const top = sec.offsetTop;
      const height = sec.offsetHeight;
      const id = sec.getAttribute('id');
      if (scrollPos >= top && scrollPos < top + height) {
        document.querySelectorAll('.rail-link').forEach(link => {
          const active = link.getAttribute('href') === `#${id}`;
          link.classList.toggle('active', active);
          if (active) link.setAttribute('aria-current', 'location');
          else link.removeAttribute('aria-current');
        });
      }
    });
  });
})();
<!-- END js/kinetic-serif.js -->

  <p><strong>Can two deployments share module code while keeping their state separate?</strong> Yes. Here, two independently run root configurations call the same module source and use distinct backend state objects.</p>

    </tbody>
  </table>
  <div class="specimen-notes">
    <p><strong>Illustrative assumptions.</strong> Both roots use the same repository revision and the <code>default</code> workspace. One pre-existing example bucket, <code>kc-state-example</code>, uses distinct prefixes <code>dev</code> and <code>prod</code>, producing <code>gs://kc-state-example/dev/default.tfstate</code> and <code>gs://kc-state-example/prod/default.tfstate</code>. These names do not identify deployed infrastructure.</p>
    <p><strong>Limits.</strong> Distinct objects separate state storage, but do not establish IAM isolation or prevent both roots from targeting the same real resource. Assume distinct resource identities and no cross-state reads for this example. State records resource mappings, not application data. A local source edit can affect both roots on their next run; sharing source does not deploy either root automatically.</p>
  </div>

## Terraform/GCS assumptions and historical source gap
Source: https://jeonkwan.github.io/kinetic-construct/reference/architecture-spec.md

<!-- BEGIN reference/architecture-spec.md -->
# Terraform/GCS specimen: shared module, separate state

This document describes the illustrative teaching model in [the working specimen](../starter/diagram.html). It is distinct from Kinetic Serif's reusable [diagram grammar](diagram-guide.md). No infrastructure was deployed or inspected to establish this example.

## Answer and modeled relationships

Two independently run root configurations, `envs/dev/cloud-sql` and `envs/prod/cloud-sql`, call `modules/cloud-sql-ha` from one repository revision. Each root's Terraform run uses its own GCS state object. The module has no independent backend simply because it has its own directory. Deployed Cloud SQL instances are deliberately omitted from the figure; the roots are configurations used for execution, not running databases.

| Root | Source | Backend bucket | Prefix | Workspace | Resulting state object |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dev | `../../../modules/cloud-sql-ha` | `kc-state-example` | `dev` | `default` | `gs://kc-state-example/dev/default.tfstate` |
| Prod | `../../../modules/cloud-sql-ha` | `kc-state-example` | `prod` | `default` | `gs://kc-state-example/prod/default.tfstate` |

Each root → source arrow means “calls source.” Each root → ledger arrow means “the Terraform run reads/writes state.” This aggregates access as a relationship, not one-way data movement. Dashed boxes group environment configuration and its state association, not a physical bucket, network, or access-control boundary.

## Verified concepts and assumptions

Checked against primary HashiCorp documentation on 2026-10-26:

- Roots call child modules; child resources are managed as part of the calling configuration. Reusing source is supported. See [modules overview](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/modules).
- GCS stores named workspace state at `<prefix>/<name>.tfstate` in a pre-existing bucket and supports state locking. Bucket, prefix, and workspace together identify the example object. See [GCS backend](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/backend/gcs).
- State maps configuration resource instances to real objects. Distinct state objects must not be assumed to safely manage the same remote object. See [purpose of state](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/state/purpose).

The exact bucket, prefixes, paths, common revision, default workspace, distinct resource identities, and absence of cross-state reads are example assumptions. Permissions, provider inputs, resource settings, networking, service accounts, encryption-key policy, bucket creation, and release automation are omitted. Code excerpts are intentionally incomplete teaching fragments, not a validated Terraform/GCP deployment.

Separate state storage does not establish IAM isolation, remove shared dependencies, or guarantee a bounded blast radius. Folder nesting alone establishes none of these. Sharing local source can affect either root on its next run; it does not automatically apply either root.

## Historical source gap and recovered policies

The reconstructed source introduced “three orthogonal planes” but did not supply the enumeration. That original passage remains unknown. The source/root/state teaching labels above are a new, explicit model for this pilot, not recovered missing text.

The four statements below were recovered from the original chat as “Architectural Laws.” They are retained here as historical project policies to review, not Terraform guarantees or universal Kinetic Serif rules:

1. **State Isolation over Folder Hierarchy.** The original said isolation was determined “solely by backend prefix and bucket IAM permissions.” Correction: bucket and workspace also affect state location; authorization and resource ownership are separate concerns.
2. **Deterministic Version Promotion.** Explicit Git commit SHAs were preferred over floating heads or mutable tags. This is a release-policy choice. The local-source pilot assumes a common checked-out revision and does not demonstrate remote source pinning.
3. **Least Privilege Blast Perimeter.** Dedicated, narrowly scoped service accounts were proposed. No such IAM policy is implemented or verified by the figure.
4. **Independent GCS State Locks.** GCS supports locking; distinct state objects avoid sharing one state lock. This does not prevent all contention, shared-resource conflicts, or partial-apply failures.
